reflection.text:
We chased dose-dependent tubulin brightening (e10 rho=+1.00, e15 rho=+0.95, e3 tub_glcm_contrast z=+42.5) and replicated multinucleation (e13 z=+10.6) into first Microtubule stabilizers 0.55 then Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.50, despite low atlas similarities 0.417-0.52 and a split NSC vote. The review correctly flagged that actin rose in parallel, cells rounded, no bundles were ever reported, and key 10uM features were unstable across replicates (e8 vs e13: tub contrast 21.9 vs 5.7, nuc_solidity -23.7 vs -3.9), prompting the re-examination in e19 that moved us from stabilizers to Aurora but still within the wrong panel.

Unblinding to ALLN, a calpain/proteasome inhibitor, explains the confound: proteasome blockade stabilizes regulatory proteins (PMID 26639105, PMID 12209081) via both calpain and ubiquitin-proteasome systems (PMID 27880847) and can cause cell death (PMID 11319608), producing enlarged high-DNA nuclei at 3uM (e2 nuc_major_axis z=+15.2) and irregular multinucleated cells that mimic mitotic failure. Our second literature search for proteasome-inhibitor multinucleation returned 0 hits, so we lacked a direct link and forced the phenotype into nearest mitotic neighbors.

Acquisition choices compounded this: only 4 wells at 3, 10, 10 and 30uM with no low-dose anchor, no washout, and no ubiquitin/proteasome readout, while the reference atlas contained no Protein degradation class to allow an out-of-panel call.
what_was_right: Recognized enlarged high-DNA nuclei at 3uM (e2) and replicated multinucleation (e13) as mitotic-exit failure rather than nonspecific toxicity
Rejected the protocol NSC Microtubule destabilizers vote (2/4 wells) because tub_mean increased with dose (e10) instead of decreasing
Correctly downgraded Microtubule stabilizers after e19 re-examination found intact unbundled microtubules with no bundles, as requested in review
what_was_wrong: Misread tub_mean and tub_glcm_contrast dose rises (e10, e15, e3, e8) as stabilized polymer while ignoring parallel act_mean rise and rounding/shrinkage confound flagged in review
Treated multinucleation plus enlarged nuclei (e2, e13) as Aurora-specific and did not consider proteasome/calpain inhibition as a cause of mitotic failure
Trusted split low-similarity atlas matches (0.417-0.52, destabilizers/DNA replication/Aurora) from a panel lacking Protein degradation instead of calling out-of-panel mechanism
Acquired only mid-high doses (3,10,10,30uM) with unstable texture/nuclear features across 10uM replicates and ordered no proteasome/ubiquitin assay to discriminate degradation blockade

citations.claim: Both calpain and ubiquitin-proteasome systems contribute to protein turnover through degradation and mTOR regulation.
Inhibition of the proteasome stabilizes E11/podoplanin protein to promote differentiation.
Proteasome-dependent regulation controls Syk tyrosine kinase levels.
Proteasome inhibitors cause cell death sensitized by pro-caspase-3 overexpression.

reflection.next_experiment: Compare ALLN to selective proteasome inhibitors (MG132/bortezomib) and a selective calpain inhibitor with ubiquitin-accumulation immunofluorescence plus a live proteasome activity assay and washout, quantifying multinucleation, nuclear solidity and tubulin texture to test protein-degradation blockade versus direct microtubule or Aurora effects.

## Reflection

We chased dose-dependent tubulin brightening (e10 rho=+1.00, e15 rho=+0.95, e3 tub_glcm_contrast z=+42.5) and replicated multinucleation (e13 z=+10.6) into first Microtubule stabilizers 0.55 then Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.50, despite low atlas similarities 0.417-0.52 and a split NSC vote. The review correctly flagged that actin rose in parallel, cells rounded, no bundles were ever reported, and key 10uM features were unstable across replicates (e8 vs e13: tub contrast 21.9 vs 5.7, nuc_solidity -23.7 vs -3.9), prompting the re-examination in e19 that moved us from stabilizers to Aurora but still within the wrong panel.

Unblinding to ALLN, a calpain/proteasome inhibitor, explains the confound: proteasome blockade stabilizes regulatory proteins (PMID 26639105, PMID 12209081) via both calpain and ubiquitin-proteasome systems (PMID 27880847) and can cause cell death (PMID 11319608), producing enlarged high-DNA nuclei at 3uM (e2 nuc_major_axis z=+15.2) and irregular multinucleated cells that mimic mitotic failure. Our second literature search for proteasome-inhibitor multinucleation returned 0 hits, so we lacked a direct link and forced the phenotype into nearest mitotic neighbors.

Acquisition choices compounded this: only 4 wells at 3, 10, 10 and 30uM with no low-dose anchor, no washout, and no ubiquitin/proteasome readout, while the reference atlas contained no Protein degradation class to allow an out-of-panel call.

What was right:
- Recognized enlarged high-DNA nuclei at 3uM (e2) and replicated multinucleation (e13) as mitotic-exit failure rather than nonspecific toxicity
- Rejected the protocol NSC Microtubule destabilizers vote (2/4 wells) because tub_mean increased with dose (e10) instead of decreasing
- Correctly downgraded Microtubule stabilizers after e19 re-examination found intact unbundled microtubules with no bundles, as requested in review

What was wrong or missed:
- Misread tub_mean and tub_glcm_contrast dose rises (e10, e15, e3, e8) as stabilized polymer while ignoring parallel act_mean rise and rounding/shrinkage confound flagged in review
- Treated multinucleation plus enlarged nuclei (e2, e13) as Aurora-specific and did not consider proteasome/calpain inhibition as a cause of mitotic failure
- Trusted split low-similarity atlas matches (0.417-0.52, destabilizers/DNA replication/Aurora) from a panel lacking Protein degradation instead of calling out-of-panel mechanism
- Acquired only mid-high doses (3,10,10,30uM) with unstable texture/nuclear features across 10uM replicates and ordered no proteasome/ubiquitin assay to discriminate degradation blockade

Proposed next experiment: Compare ALLN to selective proteasome inhibitors (MG132/bortezomib) and a selective calpain inhibitor with ubiquitin-accumulation immunofluorescence plus a live proteasome activity assay and washout, quantifying multinucleation, nuclear solidity and tubulin texture to test protein-degradation blockade versus direct microtubule or Aurora effects.
